drafts.title: API Usage Policy
drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This policy defines how PlantAtHome (operated by Silvestrix Green LLP) application programming interfaces (APIs) may be accessed and used. It protects customer data, catalogue and pricing integrity, and platform availability across the storefront, admin panel, mobile app, vendor integrations, and delivery-partner services.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all PlantAtHome APIs, including the core commerce API, the v1 modular API, delivery and shipping microservices, and inbound webhooks from external partners (payment gateway, courier partners, WhatsApp notification gateway). It covers internal engineers, contractors, approved nursery vendors, and third-party partners granted API access.

3. Definitions

  • Internal Consumer: a PlantAtHome-owned client (storefront, admin, mobile app, background workers).
  • Partner Consumer: an external system (courier partner, payment gateway, vendor system) exchanging data with PlantAtHome APIs.
  • API Credential: any key, token, or signing secret used to authenticate a consumer or verify a webhook.

4. Access and Authentication

  • Every consumer must authenticate with its own credential. Shared or team-wide keys are prohibited.
  • User-facing sessions use short-lived personal access tokens; machine-to-machine calls use dedicated service credentials scoped to the minimum required endpoints.
  • All inbound webhooks (payment confirmations, courier status callbacks) must be verified by signature or shared-secret HMAC before processing. Unsigned callbacks may only be treated as triggers to fetch authoritative data over an authenticated channel, never as authoritative data themselves.
  • Access is granted on least-privilege: vendor integrations see only their own products, inventory, and orders.

5. Key Management

  • Credentials are issued and revoked only by the Technology team, recorded in an access register.
  • Credentials live in the secrets store or environment configuration — never in source code, tickets, chat, or client-side bundles.
  • Credentials are rotated on suspected compromise, on departure of any person who had access, and on partner contract termination. Revocation target: within 24 hours (configurable).

6. Rate Limits

Default limits below are DRAFT and configurable; production values are maintained in platform configuration.

Consumer classDefault limitNotes
Public storefront (unauthenticated)60 requests/min per IPCatalogue browse, search
Authenticated customer120 requests/min per accountCart, checkout, orders
Vendor/partner integration300 requests/min per credentialInventory sync, order fetch
Bulk import/exportScheduled batch windows onlyRequires Technology approval

Rate limiting for authentication endpoints must key on account or credential identifiers, not raw client IP, because production traffic passes through proxies.

7. Prohibited Use

  • Scraping or bulk-extracting the plant catalogue, pricing, vendor, or availability data for resale or competitive use.
  • Bypassing city availability gates, catalogue gates, or pricing/margin logic.
  • Sharing, embedding, or exposing credentials in public repositories or client applications.
  • Load or penetration testing against production without written Technology approval.
  • Retaining customer personal data received via API beyond the purpose and period agreed in writing.

8. Responsibilities

  • Technology: issues credentials, enforces limits, monitors usage, revokes access.
  • Vendor Operations: ensures vendor integration agreements reference this policy.
  • All consumers: report suspected credential compromise immediately per the Incident Response Plan.

9. Compliance

Violations may result in throttling, suspension, or permanent revocation of access, contractual remedies for partners, and disciplinary action for employees. Suspected data misuse is handled under the Incident Response Plan and applicable Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

drafts.title: Accessibility Statement
drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This statement records PlantAtHome's commitment, as operated by Silvestrix Green LLP, to making its website and mobile app usable by as many people as possible, including people with visual, auditory, motor, and cognitive disabilities, and tells users how to report accessibility problems.

Scope

Covers the PlantAtHome customer website and mobile app, including product browsing, plant detail pages, cart and checkout, order tracking, the account area, and support entry points. Internal admin tools and vendor portals are covered by internal standards and are improved on a separate track.

Our Commitment

Buying a plant should not require perfect eyesight or a mouse. We aim for an experience where product information, prices, delivery options, and checkout are perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust for everyone, including users of screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, voice control, and magnification.

Standards We Aim For

  • We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA. This is a target we are actively working toward, not yet a claim of full conformance.
  • Our approach is also informed by the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and applicable Indian guidance on accessible ICT.

What We Do in Practice

  • Descriptive alternative text for product images, with particular care on plant photos where the image carries real information (size, pot, foliage condition).
  • Sufficient colour contrast in the design system, and meaning never conveyed by colour alone (e.g., stock status and order states carry text labels, not just colour).
  • Keyboard operability for navigation, filters, cart, and checkout, with visible focus indicators and a logical focus order.
  • Form fields at checkout with proper labels and clear, specific error messages, including address and payment steps handled through Razorpay's checkout.
  • Support for text resizing and reflow without loss of content or function on mobile and desktop.
  • Voice search as an alternative input method for finding plants.
  • Accessibility review as part of design and code review for new storefront features.

Known Limitations (DRAFT — maintained as a living list)

  • Some older product images and third-party embedded content (e.g., payment or map widgets) may not yet meet our alt-text and contrast targets.
  • Some interactive components in newer features may have incomplete screen-reader announcements while remediation is in progress.
  • PDF invoices may not yet be fully tagged for screen readers; a support agent can provide order details in an accessible format on request.

Feedback and Contact for Accessibility Issues

  • If you encounter an accessibility barrier on PlantAtHome, please tell us via the support channels published on our Contact page — WhatsApp, email, or phone. Mention "Accessibility" and describe the page, what you were trying to do, and the assistive technology and browser or device you were using.
  • We aim to acknowledge accessibility reports within 2 business days and to provide a resolution or workaround within 15 business days (DRAFT targets — configurable), prioritising barriers that block ordering, payment, or order tracking.
  • If a barrier prevents you from completing a purchase, our support team will help you complete it by phone or WhatsApp in the meantime.

Responsibilities

  • Technology: owns technical conformance, audits, and remediation backlog.
  • Customer Experience: receives and triages accessibility reports and provides assisted-ordering support.
  • Compliance: reviews this statement at least annually and after major storefront releases.

Compliance

This statement is reviewed against WCAG 2.1 AA progress and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Audit findings and remediation status are tracked internally, and this statement is updated when the position materially changes.

Purpose

To govern how company assets of Silvestrix Green LLP (PlantAtHome) are issued, recorded, cared for, returned, and accounted for when lost or damaged.

Scope

All company-owned property issued to or used by employees and contractors, including laptops, phones and SIMs, headsets, barcode/label printers, packing and warehouse equipment, plant-care tools, ID cards, access cards and keys, and software licences or system accounts tied to an individual.

Definitions

  • Asset: any company property with an asset tag or issuance record, physical or digital.
  • Custodian: the employee to whom an asset is issued and who is accountable for it.

Issuance and Record

  • Every asset is issued against a signed (physical or digital) issuance record in the asset register maintained by the Technology team (IT assets) or the office/warehouse administrator (other assets), capturing: asset tag, description and serial number, custodian, issue date, condition at issue, and expected return trigger (exit, role change, or project end).
  • No asset changes hands informally: transfers between employees must be re-recorded, or the original custodian remains accountable.
  • Laptops are issued pre-configured per the Information Security Policy (encryption, endpoint protection, RBAC accounts); custodians must not alter these controls.
  • SIMs and phone numbers used for customer or vendor contact belong to the company; the number stays with the company on exit.

Care and Acceptable Use

  • Assets are for business use; incidental personal use of a laptop or phone is acceptable if it does not breach the Code of Conduct, Information Security Policy, or licences.
  • Keep assets physically secure: do not leave laptops in vehicles or unattended in public; store warehouse equipment in designated places after shifts.
  • Do not lend company assets to non-employees, including family members and delivery partners.
  • Report faults promptly; do not attempt hardware repairs yourself — the Technology team arranges service.
  • Reasonable wear and tear is expected; negligence (e.g. liquid damage, repeated loss) is not.

Return on Exit or Role Change

  • All assets must be returned on or before the last working day, or within 3 working days of a role change that ends the need, in working condition with accessories (chargers, cables) issued with them.
  • The People team's exit clearance is complete only when the asset register shows every issued item returned and the Technology team confirms account and access revocation.
  • Company data on returned devices is wiped by the Technology team; employees must not wipe devices themselves before return, so business records are preserved.
  • Unreturned or damaged-beyond-wear assets may be recovered at depreciated value from final settlement, per the employment agreement and applicable law.

Loss, Theft, and Damage Reporting

  • Report a lost or stolen asset to your manager and the Technology team within 4 hours (DRAFT — configurable) so accounts, SIMs, and access can be blocked — a lost laptop or phone is a security incident under the Information Security Policy, not just a property matter.
  • For theft, file a police report where the company advises, and share the acknowledgment for the register.
  • Accidental damage honestly reported is generally not penalised; concealment or gross negligence may lead to recovery and disciplinary action.

Responsibilities

  • Custodians: safeguard, use properly, report issues, return on time.
  • Technology team / administrators: maintain the register, configure and wipe devices, run an annual physical verification (DRAFT — configurable).
  • Managers and People team: trigger returns on exit or role change and enforce clearance.

Compliance

Failure to return assets, unreported loss, or misuse may result in recovery of value, disciplinary action up to termination, and legal action where warranted.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This policy ensures PlantAtHome can recover business-critical data — orders, payments, customer accounts, the plant catalogue, vendor and inventory records, and product media — after accidental deletion, corruption, hardware failure, or a security incident.

2. Scope

All production data stores operated by or for PlantAtHome. Staging data is backed up on a best-effort basis only, except where staging shares a resource with production (notably the shared media bucket), in which case production rules apply to that resource.

3. Backup Scope

AssetContentsCriticality
Production databaseOrders, payments references, customers, catalogue, inventory, vendor records, settings, integration configurationCritical
Media object storageProduct images, plant photos, category banners, uploaded documents (vendor KYC, invoices)Critical
Application configurationEnvironment configuration and secrets (backed up via the secrets store, not in DB dumps)High
Code and infrastructure definitionsGit repositories, CI workflowsCovered by hosted VCS redundancy

4. Frequency and Retention

Values below are DRAFT and configurable.

AssetFrequencyRetention
Database — automated snapshotDaily30 days
Database — logical dump (off-host copy)Daily90 days
Database — monthly archiveMonthly12 months (finance/GST support)
Media bucketContinuous replication or daily sync to a separate backup bucket90 days of deleted-object recovery
  • Because the media bucket currently has no object versioning and is shared between staging and production, enabling versioning or cross-bucket replication is a priority remediation; until then, all deletes must go through the designated media service, and bulk deletes require Technology approval.
  • At least one backup copy must reside outside the primary production host and account boundary, so a single host or account compromise cannot destroy both live data and backups.
  • Backups containing customer personal data are encrypted at rest and access-restricted to the Technology team.

5. Restore Testing

  • Quarterly restore test: once per quarter, Technology restores the latest database backup into an isolated environment and verifies row counts, most recent order timestamps, and application boot against the restored data.
  • A media restore test (recover a sample of objects to a scratch prefix) is performed in the same quarterly exercise.
  • Each test is recorded with date, backup used, time-to-restore, and issues found. A failed test is treated as a High-severity finding and remediated before the next cycle.

6. Backup Failure Handling

  • Backup jobs must alert on failure. Two consecutive failed daily backups escalate to the Technology lead the same day.
  • Backups are verified for non-zero size and completion status automatically; silent success without verification does not count as a backup.

7. Responsibilities

  • Technology: operates backup jobs, monitors alerts, runs quarterly restore tests, maintains the restore runbook.
  • Finance: confirms retention meets GST and audit record-keeping needs.
  • Compliance: reviews retention against data-protection obligations annually.

8. Compliance

Retention must satisfy Indian tax and audit requirements while not retaining personal data longer than necessary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Deviations from this policy require documented approval by Technology leadership.

drafts.title: Business Continuity Plan
drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

Defines how PlantAtHome keeps serving customers — or degrades gracefully and recovers — when a major disruption hits. Live plants are perishable: unlike general e-commerce, an order that waits three days is often a dead product, so continuity planning prioritises fast rerouting and honest customer communication over holding orders.

Scope

Covers disruptions to order intake, fulfilment (direct and vendor nurseries), delivery (hyperlocal and courier lanes), payments and customer communication. Activation and step-by-step execution are in the Contingency Procedures SOP; this plan defines scenarios, strategies and recovery objectives.

Planning Assumptions

  • Multiple delivery partners exist per lane (hyperlocal and courier), so single-partner failure is survivable by rerouting.
  • Vendor nurseries are geographically distributed; the master catalog can be gated per city so unavailable stock stops selling within hours.
  • WhatsApp, email and phone provide redundant customer-contact channels; Razorpay payment links allow order capture even if checkout is degraded.

Scenarios and Contingencies

Scenario 1: Courier Partner Outage

A courier or hyperlocal partner suspends pickups (technical outage, serviceability withdrawal, strike). Contingency: reroute bookings to alternate partners on the same lane; pause new orders only for pincodes with no alternate coverage; for already-packed live plants, prioritise re-booking within 24 hours or return stock to vendor care to prevent mortality; notify affected customers via WhatsApp with revised ETAs.

Scenario 2: Severe Weather Event

Heatwave, cold wave, monsoon flooding or storm makes transit unsafe for live plants or blocks delivery in a city. Contingency: apply the city gate to pause plant dispatch to affected areas (hardy goods like pots and tools may continue where couriers operate); hold plants at vendor nurseries where they can be watered and shaded rather than in transit hubs; batch-notify customers with the option of waiting, substituting, or a full refund; resume with a backlog-clearing dispatch plan that ships oldest orders first.

Scenario 3: Loss of a Key Vendor Nursery

A high-volume vendor exits, fails quality standards, or suffers stock loss (disease, flooding). Contingency: immediately mark the vendor's SKUs unavailable in affected cities; reassign open orders to alternate vendors carrying equivalent SKUs, accepting reasonable natural variation with customer consent; where no substitute exists, refund proactively before the customer complains; trigger accelerated onboarding of a replacement vendor per Vendor Operations procedures.

Scenario 4: Platform Outage

Website/app, API or hosting infrastructure is down; orders cannot be placed or managed. Contingency: switch order intake to manual capture via WhatsApp and phone with Razorpay payment links per the Contingency Procedures; publish a status notice on available channels; continue fulfilling already-confirmed orders from exported order lists; reconcile all manual orders into the platform on restoration before normal reporting resumes.

Recovery Objectives

FunctionRecovery Time Objective (DRAFT — configurable)Interim mode
Customer communication2 hoursWhatsApp/phone/email
Order intake8 hoursManual capture + payment links
Dispatch (unaffected lanes)24 hoursAlternate partner rerouting
Full platform operations72 hoursBacklog clearance plan

Testing and Maintenance

The plan is exercised at least annually (DRAFT — configurable) via a tabletop walkthrough of one scenario, and reviewed after every real activation, new city launch, or partner change. Lessons feed the risk register.

Responsibilities

  • Management: declares a continuity event and approves customer-compensation decisions.
  • Logistics Head: partner rerouting and dispatch decisions.
  • Vendor Operations Head: vendor substitution and stock-holding decisions.
  • Technology Head: platform recovery and manual-order reconciliation.
  • Customer Experience Head: customer notifications and refund handling.

Compliance

Every activation is logged with timeline, decisions and customer impact, and reviewed within 10 working days. Refund and communication commitments in published customer policies continue to apply during disruptions.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This policy sets out when a customer may cancel an order on PlantAtHome, what charges (if any) apply, and how cancellations are processed across PlantAtHome-fulfilled and vendor-nursery-fulfilled orders on both hyperlocal and courier delivery lanes.

Scope

Applies to all customer orders placed through PlantAtHome channels, including prepaid (Razorpay) and cash-on-delivery orders, single-vendor and multi-vendor orders, and corporate gifting orders unless a separate corporate agreement states otherwise.

Definitions

  • Vendor-allocated: the order (or a line item) has been assigned to an approved nursery vendor for fulfilment.
  • Picked: the vendor or PlantAtHome warehouse has packed the item and a pickup has been scheduled with a hyperlocal or courier partner.
  • Dispatched: the shipment has been handed to the delivery partner and is in transit.

Cancellation Rules by Order Status

Fee values below are DRAFT and configurable by Operations.

Order statusCustomer cancellationChargeNotes
Placed (payment confirmed, not yet allocated)Allowed — self-service in the app or websiteNone; full refundInstant confirmation via WhatsApp and email.
Vendor-allocatedAllowed via Customer ExperienceNone; full refundVendor is notified and the allocation is released.
Picked (packed, pickup booked)Allowed on request, subject to the pickup being stopped in timeNone if pickup stopped; otherwise treated as dispatchedLive plants are packed to order, so requests at this stage are time-critical.
Dispatched (in transit)Not cancellable—Customer may refuse delivery; the case is then handled as a return, and forward shipping (DRAFT: capped at ₹150) may be deducted from the refund. Live plants refused in transit are assessed for viability on return before refund.
DeliveredNot cancellable—Handled under the Replacement Policy or Refund Policy as applicable.

Customized and Made-to-Order Products

  • Customized items — engraved or branded planters, curated corporate gifting hampers, made-to-order plant arrangements — are cancellable only while the order is in Placed status, before customization work begins.
  • Once customization has started, cancellation is at PlantAtHome's discretion and may attract a charge up to the cost of work completed (DRAFT: up to 50% of item value, configurable).
  • FarmBox fresh produce orders are cancellable up to the daily packing cut-off (DRAFT: 6:00 AM on the delivery day, configurable) because produce is harvested and packed against confirmed orders.

Partial Cancellation

In multi-item or multi-vendor orders, individual line items may be cancelled following the same status rules per item. Refunds are computed at line-item level per the Refund Policy, with delivery charges retained where the remaining shipment still ships.

Cancellation by PlantAtHome

PlantAtHome may cancel an order or line item for stock unavailability, plant health failing pre-dispatch quality checks, weather conditions unsafe for live-plant transit, serviceability changes, pricing errors, or suspected fraud. In such cases the customer is notified on WhatsApp and refunded in full within the Refund Policy timelines, with no charge.

Responsibilities

  • Customer Experience: handles cancellation requests, confirms status cut-offs, communicates outcomes.
  • Vendor Operations: releases vendor allocations and stops pickups on cancelled orders.
  • Logistics: attempts pickup interception for Picked-status cancellations.
  • Finance: processes refunds and GST credit notes.

Compliance

This policy is intended to align with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. Cancellation charges, where applied, are disclosed before order confirmation.

drafts.title: Change Management Policy
drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This policy governs how changes reach PlantAtHome production systems — application code, database schema and data operations, infrastructure, environment configuration, and third-party integration settings — so that a plant ordered today is still deliverable tomorrow.

2. Scope

All production-affecting changes across the commerce API, storefront, admin panel, mobile app backends, delivery microservices, CI/CD workflows, and integration credentials (payment, courier, WhatsApp). It applies to employees and contractors alike.

3. Standard Change Flow (Staging-First)

  • Branch and review: work happens on a branch; every change to a main branch goes through a pull request. No direct pushes to main for production-affecting repositories.
  • Staging deployment: changes deploy to staging via the CI pipeline and are verified there against staging's sandbox partner credentials before any production promotion. "It works locally" is not a gate; staging is.
  • Verification on staging: the author verifies the actual user-visible behaviour (a test checkout, a courier quote, an admin action) — not merely a green build. Deployment success and live behaviour are checked separately; a green pipeline is not proof the new code is serving.
  • Production promotion: production deploys run only through the approved promotion workflow (CI dispatch with explicit confirmation input), never by manual edits on production hosts. The promoter confirms the deployed commit matches the intended one after dispatch.

4. Review Gates

Change typeMinimum gate (DRAFT, configurable)
Routine code change1 reviewer approval + CI green + staging verification
Database migration / bulk data operation1 reviewer + tested rollback path + fresh backup confirmed before running
Payment, pricing, or checkout logic2 reviewers, one being a senior engineer; test order on staging
Secrets / integration credentialsTechnology lead approval; worker restart included in the change
Infrastructure (hosts, DNS, CDN, buckets)Technology lead approval + written rollback note

5. Production Promotion Approvals

  • Promotions are performed during business hours where possible; avoid promoting immediately before high-order windows (weekend mornings, campaign launches) unless the change fixes an active problem.
  • The promoter must be reachable for 60 minutes after promotion and must watch error rates and order flow during that window.
  • Batched promotions list every included change; "mystery deploys" of accumulated unreviewed work are prohibited.

6. Rollback Expectations

  • Every production change must have a stated rollback path before promotion: redeploy previous commit, revert migration, restore configuration value, or feature-flag off.
  • Risky or user-visible features ship behind flags defaulting off, enabling rollback without a deploy.
  • Irreversible operations (destructive data changes, deletes in shared storage) require a verified backup taken immediately beforehand and Technology lead sign-off.
  • If production degrades after a change and the cause is not identified within 30 minutes (configurable), roll back first and investigate second.

7. Emergency Changes

  • During a declared SEV1/SEV2 incident, the Incident Commander may authorize an expedited change with a single reviewer (or post-hoc review if no reviewer is available).
  • Every emergency change is documented in the incident timeline and receives normal review retroactively within 2 business days.

8. Change Records

The pull request, CI run, and promotion dispatch together form the change record: what changed, who reviewed, who promoted, and when. These records are retained with the repository history.

9. Responsibilities

  • Authors: staging verification, rollback plan, post-promotion watch.
  • Reviewers: genuine review of correctness and blast radius, not rubber-stamping.
  • Technology lead: approves elevated-risk gates, owns the promotion workflow.

10. Compliance

Bypassing gates or editing production directly outside a declared incident is a policy violation and is reviewed by Technology leadership. Repeated violations follow the disciplinary process.

DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This policy defines how PlantAtHome computes platform commission on vendor-fulfilled orders: the base rate, category modifiers, treatment of promotions and discounts, and rounding — so that vendor settlements are predictable, auditable, and consistent with vendor agreements.

Scope

Applies to all line items fulfilled by approved nursery vendors and suppliers across all verticals. It does not apply to items fulfilled from PlantAtHome's own inventory. Delivery fees are outside commission and handled under the delivery pricing rules.

Commission Structure

Commission is computed per line item on the item's commissionable base (defined below), as base rate plus a category modifier. All rates below are DRAFT and configurable in the commission master; the signed vendor agreement prevails where it specifies different rates.

CategoryBase rateCategory modifierEffective rate (DRAFT)
Live plants15%+0%15%
Pots and planters15%+3%18%
Gardening tools and accessories15%+3%18%
Seeds and fertilizers15%-3%12%
FarmBox fresh produce15%-5%10%

Commissionable Base

  • The base is the item's selling price actually charged to the customer (before GST), after item-level discounts.
  • City-level margins applied by the platform's pricing engine are platform revenue and are excluded from the vendor's base; commission applies to the vendor transfer value component per the vendor agreement.
  • GST is never commissioned: commission applies to the pre-tax value.

Promotions Treatment

  • Platform-funded promotions (site-wide coupons, seasonal sales funded by PlantAtHome): commission is computed on the price before the platform-funded discount, so the vendor is not penalized for platform marketing.
  • Vendor-funded promotions (vendor opts into a discount): commission is computed on the discounted price the customer paid.
  • Co-funded promotions: the discount is split per the campaign terms; each party's share adjusts the base accordingly.

DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

Gives PlantAtHome teams the concrete steps to execute when the Business Continuity Plan is activated: who decides, who tells whom, and exactly how orders keep moving by hand when systems or partners are down.

Scope

Applies to all continuity activations under the Business Continuity Plan scenarios (courier outage, severe weather, key vendor loss, platform outage) and to partial activations affecting a single city or lane.

Activation Criteria

  • Any of the following triggers an activation assessment (DRAFT thresholds — configurable): order placement or checkout down for more than 30 minutes; a delivery partner rejecting bookings across a lane for more than 2 hours; a weather alert making live-plant transit unsafe in a serviced city; a vendor covering a material share of open orders becoming unable to fulfil.
  • The on-call Logistics lead assesses against these criteria and recommends activation; only Management (a Designated Partner) declares an activation, and may declare it city-scoped or company-wide.
  • The declaration is logged with time, scenario, scope and the named incident coordinator.

Communications Tree

  • Incident coordinator (default: Logistics Head) notifies, in order: Management, Technology Head, Vendor Operations Head, Customer Experience Head, Finance Head.
  • Each head cascades to their own team within 30 minutes and confirms back to the coordinator.
  • Customer Experience owns all outbound customer messaging: a holding message within 2 hours of activation, then updates at least every 12 hours until stand-down, via WhatsApp first, email as backup.
  • Vendor Operations notifies affected nursery vendors with hold/water-and-hold instructions for packed live plants.
  • No individual posts publicly about the incident; external statements are approved by Management.

Temporary Manual Order Handling

  • Order capture: during a platform outage, orders are taken via WhatsApp and phone into a controlled manual order sheet (one per day, access-restricted) recording: customer name, contact, delivery address and pincode, items, quantities, quoted price including GST, and delivery lane.
  • Payment: payment is collected only via Razorpay payment links generated per order; no bank-transfer requests to personal accounts, no card details taken over phone or chat. COD is offered only on lanes where the active partner supports it.
  • Stock check: before confirming, the agent confirms availability with the fulfilling vendor or warehouse by phone/WhatsApp — the live availability gate is down, so nothing is promised unchecked.
  • Dispatch: Logistics books deliveries directly on partner dashboards, recording the booking reference against the manual order row.
  • Invoicing: GST-compliant invoices for manual orders are issued within the platform after restoration; Finance keeps the manual sheet as the source for this.
  • Reconciliation: on stand-down, Technology and Finance enter every manual order into the platform, match Razorpay payments to orders, and resolve any mismatch before the incident is closed. The manual sheet is then archived, not deleted.

Stand-down

  • Management declares stand-down when normal systems and lanes are verified working and the manual backlog is reconciled.
  • The incident coordinator completes a post-incident report (timeline, customer impact, refunds issued, what failed, what to fix) within 10 working days; fixes are raised in the Corrective Action Process.

Responsibilities

  • Management: activation and stand-down decisions, external statements.
  • Logistics Head (incident coordinator): runs the comms tree, partner rerouting, dispatch during the incident.
  • Customer Experience: customer messaging and refund handling.
  • Technology and Finance: restoration, manual-order reconciliation, invoicing.

Compliance

Manual order sheets contain personal data and are handled per DPDP obligations: access-restricted, used only for fulfilment, archived securely. Any deviation from these procedures during an incident is recorded in the post-incident report.

Purpose

Defines a single process for raising, owning, tracking and verifiably closing corrective actions arising from internal audits, compliance reviews, customer grievances, vendor disputes, delivery incidents and regulatory changes at PlantAtHome.

Scope

Applies to all corrective and preventive actions across departments — for example: fixing GST invoice defects, correcting product-page disclosures, remediating a vendor nursery's repeated plant-quality failures, patching an access-control gap in the admin panel, or changing packing standards after transit-damage complaints.

Definitions

  • CAP: a Corrective Action record with source, owner, due date and verification evidence.
  • Containment: an immediate step that stops ongoing harm before the root cause is fixed (e.g. delisting an affected SKU, pausing a vendor, disabling a broken flow).

Process

1. Raise

  • Anyone may raise a CAP. Each record states: source (audit finding, complaint, incident, regulatory change), description, affected process or SKU/vendor, and severity (Critical / Major / Minor).

2. Own

  • The Compliance Officer assigns one named owner — the department head accountable for the affected process. Shared ownership is not permitted; supporting contributors are listed separately.

3. Due Date

  • Default due dates by severity (DRAFT — configurable): Critical 10 working days, Major 30 days, Minor 60 days.
  • One extension may be granted by the Compliance Officer with a written reason; further extensions need management approval.

4. Verify

  • Where the source was an audit finding, the auditor performs the verification per the Internal Audit SOP.

5. Close

  • Recurring CAPs on the same root cause within 12 months are escalated to management with a preventive-action review.

Purpose

To standardize intercity courier shipping through the Shiprocket aggregation platform, from booking and AWB assignment through label, manifest, pickup, tracking, and exception handling, so that live plants and gardening products move on predictable transit windows with full documentation.

Definitions

Booking and Courier Selection

  • Booking is triggered when a shipment group is packed and QC-signed per the Packaging Manual. Auto-booking applies at payment success (prepaid) or order confirmation (COD); manual booking is available in the admin console.
  • Serviceability and rates are quoted per destination pincode; courier selection favours the shortest transit window for live-plant shipments and the lowest landed cost for hard goods (DRAFT rule, configurable).

  • The shipping label (AWB-keyed) is printed and affixed on the largest flat face of the carton; live-plant orientation arrows and fragile labels must remain visible and uncovered.
  • The GST tax invoice (order-keyed) is placed in a document pouch on the carton or linked digitally as the courier requires.
  • A manifest is generated per courier per pickup location per day; the pickup executive signs it and one copy is retained for seven years with shipping records (DRAFT retention, configurable).

Pickup

  • Pickup requests are raised at booking for next-available slot; cartons must be staged and manifest-ready 60 minutes before the slot (DRAFT, configurable).
  • Missed pickups are rebooked immediately; two consecutive missed pickups on a lane escalate to the logistics lead and may trigger courier reselection.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This plan defines how PlantAtHome restores the commerce platform after a major failure, so customers can order plants, vendors can fulfil, and deliveries can be booked again within agreed targets. It complements, and depends on, the Backup Policy.

2. Scope

Production systems: the commerce API and database, storefront and admin applications, delivery and shipping microservices, media storage and CDN, queue workers, and the notification gateway (WhatsApp/email). Third-party outages (payment gateway, courier partners) are handled operationally, not by this plan, but degraded-mode behaviour is noted below.

3. Recovery Objectives

Targets below are DRAFT and configurable; they reflect a lean single-region deployment.

ServiceRTO (restore within)RPO (max data loss)
Production database4 hours24 hours (daily backup); target 1 hour once point-in-time recovery is enabled
Commerce API + storefront4 hoursNone (stateless, redeploy from Git)
Admin panel8 hoursNone (stateless)
Media storage/CDN8 hours24 hours for newly uploaded media
Delivery microservices8 hoursRe-derivable from partner APIs (authenticated Track is authority)
Notifications (WhatsApp/email)24 hoursAcceptable to lose queued notifications; orders remain intact

4. Scenario: Database Loss or Corruption

  • Declare an incident (SEV1) per the Incident Response Plan; place the storefront into maintenance mode to stop writes against bad data.
  • Identify the last known-good backup (daily snapshot or logical dump per the Backup Policy).
  • Restore into a fresh database instance; never restore over the damaged instance until a forensic copy is preserved.
  • Verify: latest order timestamps, payment records against gateway dashboard, inventory counts on a sample of products.
  • Repoint application configuration, restart queue workers, lift maintenance mode.
  • Reconcile the gap window: replay payment webhooks from the gateway dashboard, re-sync courier statuses via authenticated tracking APIs, and contact affected customers via WhatsApp/email for orders placed in the lost window.

5. Scenario: Production Host Loss

  • The primary compute host is a single box; its loss takes down API, cache, and workers together.
  • Provision a replacement host from the documented build steps (runbook: production host build), restore environment configuration from the secrets store, and deploy the current release via the CI/CD workflow.
  • Attach to the existing database if intact; otherwise proceed to the database-loss scenario.
  • Re-establish the local cache/queue service and restart workers; verify checkout end-to-end with a test order before announcing recovery.

6. Scenario: Region Outage

  • A full cloud-region outage exceeds current architecture; the documented posture is wait-and-communicate for outages under 12 hours (configurable), with status updates to customers and vendors via WhatsApp broadcast and social channels.
  • Beyond 12 hours, Technology leadership decides on cross-region restoration using off-host backup copies: new database from the latest off-host dump, application redeploy, DNS cutover. Expected RTO in this mode: 24-48 hours.
  • Media served via CDN continues from edge caches during origin outage, softening customer impact.

7. Degraded Modes

  • Payment gateway down: checkout paused with clear messaging; no cash-on-delivery expansion without Finance approval.
  • Courier partners down: bookings queue for retry; hyperlocal lanes and courier lanes fail independently.

8. Runbook Pointers

  • Database restore runbook — maintained alongside the Backup Policy restore-test records.
  • Production host build runbook — server provisioning, web server and PHP configuration, cache service setup.
  • Deployment/promotion runbook — see Change Management Policy.
  • Incident communications templates — see Incident Response Plan.

9. Testing and Maintenance

The database-loss scenario is exercised via the quarterly restore test. A tabletop walkthrough of host-loss and region-outage scenarios is run annually. This plan is reviewed after every SEV1 incident.

10. Responsibilities

  • Technology: owns execution, runbooks, and testing.
  • Customer Experience: customer and vendor communications during recovery.
  • Leadership: region-failover and extended-outage decisions.

11. Compliance

Recovery actions must preserve financial records for GST compliance and follow the Incident Response Plan for any incident with a security or personal-data dimension.

Purpose

To define how PlantAtHome handles failed delivery attempts on both hyperlocal and courier lanes — maximizing successful reattempts, minimizing return-to-origin (RTO) losses, and protecting live plants that cannot survive extended limbo in a courier network.

Scope

Applies to all outbound shipments where a delivery attempt fails: customer unreachable, address issues, customer refusal, COD not ready, or premises closed. Customer-initiated returns after successful delivery follow the Reverse Logistics SOP.

Definitions

  • NDR: non-delivery report from the courier recording a failed attempt and reason.
  • RTO: return to origin — the shipment travels back to the dispatch point.
  • Contact ladder: the escalating sequence of customer contact channels and timings.

Delivery Attempts

  • Hyperlocal: one rider attempt per booking; the rider waits up to 10 minutes at the drop point while operations attempts contact (DRAFT, configurable). A failed hyperlocal attempt returns the package to the pickup point the same day — it never sits overnight with a rider.
  • Courier: up to 3 attempts per courier norms (DRAFT, configurable); every NDR must receive a PlantAtHome response (reattempt instruction or updated address) within 24 hours or the courier defaults to RTO.

Customer Contact Ladder (DRAFT, configurable)

StepChannelTiming
1WhatsApp notification with reattempt/address-update optionsWithin 1 h of failed attempt / NDR
2Phone call from Customer ExperienceWithin 4 business hours if no WhatsApp response
3Second call + SMS and email fallbackNext business day
4Final notice: reattempt deadline and RTO consequence24 h before NDR response deadline

Reattempt / RTO Decision Tree

  • Customer responds with reattempt or corrected address: instruct reattempt; hyperlocal failures are rebooked as a fresh partner booking.
  • Customer refuses delivery: accept RTO; prepaid orders follow the refund rules in the published cancellation policy; COD refusal is recorded against the customer's order history.
  • No response by the final notice deadline: shipments containing live plants — accept RTO immediately rather than letting plants die in further attempts; hard goods only — one final reattempt where the courier allows, then RTO.
  • Address unserviceable after correction: RTO, and Customer Experience offers reshipment at a serviceable address with any applicable charges quoted before rebooking.
  • All RTO decisions above a value threshold of INR 3,000 (DRAFT, configurable) require ops-lead approval.

Plant-Survival Triage on RTO

  • Every returned live plant is inspected within 24 hours of arrival at the dispatch point.
  • Grade A (healthy): re-water, recover for 48 hours, return to sellable inventory.
  • Grade B (stressed but recoverable): move to the nursery recovery area; re-grade after 7 days; sellable only after passing the inventory health check (DRAFT durations, configurable).
  • Grade C (unrecoverable): write off with photo evidence; the loss is attributed per the responsibility matrix — courier claim if transit exceeded the Live Plant Shipping SOP window, vendor debit if pre-dispatch condition caused it, or absorbed as RTO cost otherwise.
  • Triage outcomes are recorded on the shipment record for RTO-loss reporting to Finance.

Responsibilities

  • Logistics operations: NDR responses, RTO decisions, triage coordination.
  • Customer Experience: the contact ladder and customer-facing outcomes.
  • Vendor Operations: triage at vendor nursery dispatch points and vendor debits.
  • Finance: refunds via Razorpay for prepaid RTOs, RTO cost reporting.

Compliance

Refund timelines and communications must satisfy the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and PlantAtHome's published cancellation and refund policy; refunds for prepaid orders are processed to the original Razorpay payment method with GST credit notes issued where an invoice was raised.

DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This policy defines what financially significant events the PlantAtHome platform must log, the immutability expected of those logs, who may access them, and how long they are retained — so that every money movement and every change to money-affecting configuration can be reconstructed after the fact.

Scope

Applies to all production systems of Silvestrix Green LLP that create, modify, or configure financial records: the commerce API, admin panel, vendor portal, payment and refund integrations (Razorpay), settlement jobs, and pricing/commission engines.

Events That Must Be Logged

  • Order lifecycle: order creation, payment capture, cancellation, delivery confirmation, and every status transition, with actor and timestamp (the platform's order-events stream).
  • Money movements: refund initiation and approval (including approver identity and matrix level), settlement postings, vendor payouts, COD remittance postings, manual ledger adjustments.
  • Configuration changes: commission rates, city-pricing margins, delivery fees, tax/HSN master entries, coupon and promotion definitions — old value, new value, actor, effective date.
  • Access and authority changes: role and permission grants affecting financial functions, vendor bank-detail changes, payout-account changes.
  • Document issuance: invoice and credit-note generation, including number-series usage.

Log Content Standard

Each entry records: timestamp (UTC and IST), actor (user ID, or system job name for automated actions), entity and identifier (order, payment ID, vendor, config key), action, before/after values where applicable, and source (admin UI, API, scheduled job, webhook). Logs must never store full card data or payment credentials; gateway references (payment ID, UTR) are used instead.

Immutability Expectation

  • Audit records are append-only: no application code path may update or delete an audit entry; corrections are made by writing a new compensating entry that references the original.
  • Database-level controls (restricted grants on audit tables) back the application-level rule; direct production writes to audit tables outside the application are prohibited.
  • Sealed operational records that serve as audit evidence (e.g., booked shipment groupings) must not be regrouped or rewritten once money or a booking is attached to them.
  • Any detected tampering or gap is a security incident and is escalated to the Technology and Finance heads the same day.

Access

RoleAccess (DRAFT, configurable)
Finance teamRead access to all financial audit logs
Technology (on-call/senior)Read access for incident investigation
Statutory/internal auditorsRead access on engagement, time-bound
All other staffNo direct access; extracts on approved request

Access is granted through the platform's RBAC system, reviewed quarterly, and every log-access grant is itself logged.

Retention

Financial audit logs are retained for a minimum of eight years (DRAFT, aligned with financial record-keeping expectations under Indian company and tax law, to be confirmed by legal counsel), in a form that remains queryable for at least the most recent two financial years, with older records archivable to durable storage. Deletion after the retention period requires Finance Head approval and a documented disposal record.

Responsibilities

  • Technology: implements logging, immutability controls, storage, archival, and RBAC enforcement.
  • Finance: defines the list of financially significant events, uses logs in reconciliations and audits.
  • Compliance: annual review that logged events, retention, and access match this policy.

New features touching money may not ship without the corresponding audit events (a control gate in the release checklist). Non-compliant gaps found in review are tracked to remediation with owner and deadline.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

To prevent transit damage to fragile items — ceramic and terracotta pots, glass planters, decor — through mandatory double-boxing, void fill, and labeling standards, and to ensure that when damage does occur PlantAtHome holds the evidence needed to recover the loss from the delivery partner.

Scope

Applies to all shipments containing ceramics, terracotta, glass, mirrors, or any SKU flagged fragile in the catalog, on both hyperlocal and courier lanes, outbound and reverse. Live plants shipped in ceramic pots must satisfy both this SOP and the Live Plant Shipping SOP.

Definitions

  • Double-boxing: the wrapped item is packed in an inner carton, which is suspended inside an outer carton with void fill on all six faces.
  • Void fill: crumpled paper, honeycomb wrap, or air pillows filling all empty space so contents cannot shift.

Packing Procedure

  • Inspect the item for pre-existing chips or hairline cracks; a flawed item never ships — return it to inventory review.
  • Wrap the item in a minimum of two full layers of bubble wrap or honeycomb paper, taping the wrap to itself, never to the item.
  • Hollow items (pots, vases): fill the cavity with crumpled paper so the walls are supported from inside.
  • Place in an inner carton with no more than 1 cm of play; fill remaining space.
  • Suspend the inner carton in the outer carton with at least 5 cm of void fill on all six faces (DRAFT, configurable).
  • Multiple fragile items in one order: each item wrapped and separated by dividers; never let two ceramic surfaces touch.
  • Perform a gentle shake test — any audible movement means repack.

Fragile Labeling

  • Affix Fragile labels on all four vertical faces and the top of the outer carton.
  • Add This Side Up arrows on all four vertical faces for items with a defined orientation.
  • Mark the courier booking as fragile where the partner supports the flag so handling surcharges and care instructions apply.
  • At hyperlocal handover, verbally instruct the rider that the package is fragile and must travel flat; refuse handover to open two-wheeler carriage without a securing crate or bag.

Claim Evidence

Weight at booking vs courier-recorded weightBooking and courier scan12 months
Customer damage photos and unboxing video where availableWithin 48 h of deliveryLife of claim + 6 months
Claim filing confirmation with partnerWithin partner claim windowLife of claim + 6 months

Customers reporting damage are asked via WhatsApp for photos of the outer carton, inner packaging, and the damaged item before any refund or replacement is approved; the Customer Experience team must never require the customer to return shards of broken glass or ceramic — photo evidence suffices and the item is disposed of safely.

Responsibilities

  • Packers and QC checkers: execute and verify the packing procedure and photo capture.
  • Logistics operations: file partner claims within the claim window and track recovery.
  • Customer Experience: collect customer evidence and trigger refund/replace per the Reverse Logistics SOP.
  • Vendor Operations: ensure vendor nurseries shipping ceramics meet this standard; repeat failures may shift packing to a PlantAtHome hub with costs debited to the vendor (DRAFT, configurable).

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This SOP defines how tax invoices, credit notes, and related GST documents are generated for PlantAtHome orders, so that every taxable supply by Silvestrix Green LLP is invoiced correctly, with the right HSN classification, and reflected accurately in GST returns.

Scope

Applies to all customer orders (B2C and B2B, including corporate gifting), across all verticals and both fulfilment lanes (hyperlocal and courier). Vendor-to-platform invoicing is covered by the Vendor Settlement Policy and vendor agreements.

Invoice Generation

  • A tax invoice is generated automatically at dispatch for each order (or suborder, where an order splits across vendors/shipments), with a unique, sequential invoice number per financial year.
  • The invoice carries: supplier GSTIN and details, place of supply, customer details, line items with HSN code, quantity, taxable value, tax rate, and CGST/SGST or IGST split based on place of supply versus the dispatching state.
  • Delivery charges collected from the customer are invoiced as a separate line with the applicable classification and rate.
  • For B2B customers who provide a GSTIN at checkout, the GSTIN is validated and printed on the invoice to enable input credit.
  • Invoices are attached to the order in the customer account and shared via email; a WhatsApp notification links to the invoice.

HSN Classification

Finance maintains a product-category-to-HSN master. Illustratively, live plants fall under Chapter 6 of the tariff, while pots, tools, seeds, and fertilizers fall under their respective chapters with differing rates — exact codes and rates per line are taken only from the approved HSN/rate master, never entered ad hoc. New product categories cannot go live until Finance assigns an HSN and rate. Mixed carts therefore produce multi-rate invoices; the platform must compute tax per line, not per cart.

E-Invoicing

If and when Silvestrix Green LLP's aggregate turnover crosses the e-invoicing threshold notified under GST law (threshold to be verified annually by Finance), B2B invoices must be registered on the Invoice Registration Portal and carry the IRN and QR code before issue. Finance reviews applicability each April and after any threshold notification, and coordinates with Technology to enable IRP integration before the effective date.

Credit Notes

  • Refunds, returns, and post-invoice price adjustments are documented by GST credit notes referencing the original invoice number and date.
  • Credit notes are generated when the refund is approved (per the Refund Approval Policy), not when the customer first complains.
  • Partial refunds (e.g., one dead plant in a multi-item order) produce line-level credit notes at the item's taxable value and tax.
  • Credit notes are issued within the timelines permitted under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 for adjustment in returns.

Returns Filing Support

Monthly, Finance extracts an invoice register and credit-note register reconciled to the ledger (per the Payment Reconciliation SOP) as the basis for GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B preparation by the company's tax advisors. Discrepancies between invoiced values and settled receipts must be explained before filing.

Responsibilities

  • Finance: HSN/rate master, invoice number series control, credit-note approval linkage, returns support, e-invoice applicability review.
  • Technology: invoice generation logic, place-of-supply and tax-split computation, sequential numbering integrity, IRP integration when applicable.
  • Customer Experience: routing customer invoice corrections (name/GSTIN errors) to Finance within the same tax period where possible.

Compliance

Invoicing follows the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and rules thereunder. Invoice and credit-note records are retained per the Financial Audit Log Policy. Manual or out-of-system invoices are prohibited except under a documented system-outage procedure approved by the Finance Manager.

  • POD: proof of delivery — a geotagged photo of the handed-over package at the drop location.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This plan defines how PlantAtHome detects, classifies, responds to, and learns from operational and security incidents affecting the platform — from a full checkout outage to a leaked credential or a courier-integration failure that strands live-plant shipments.

2. Scope

All production incidents: availability, data integrity, security, personal-data exposure, payment processing, and delivery-integration failures. Staging-only issues are not incidents unless they risk production (e.g., a shared media bucket).

3. Severity Matrix

Classification is by customer and business impact, not by which system broke. Values are DRAFT and configurable.

SeverityDefinitionExamplesResponse startUpdates
SEV1Platform down or money/data at riskCheckout or payments failing for all users; database corruption; confirmed data breach; payment key compromiseImmediately, all handsEvery 30 min internally; customer notice within 1 hour
SEV2Major function degraded, workaround poorCourier booking failing on all lanes (live plants time-sensitive); OTP login down; admin panel down at peak hoursWithin 30 minEvery 2 hours
SEV3Partial degradation, workaround existsOne courier partner failing (others bookable); WhatsApp notifications delayed; slow product listingsSame business dayDaily
SEV4Minor issue, no material customer impactCosmetic defects; a single vendor's inventory sync erroringWithin 3 business daysOn resolution

4. Roles

  • Incident Commander (IC): the first responding engineer until handed off; owns decisions, delegates, and keeps the timeline. There is exactly one IC at a time.
  • Responders: engineers working the technical fix under the IC.
  • Communications Lead: Customer Experience representative who owns customer, vendor, and delivery-partner messaging (WhatsApp, email, storefront banner) so responders are not interrupted.
  • Leadership: informed on all SEV1/SEV2; approves external breach notifications and refunds at scale.

5. Response Steps

  • Detect and declare: anyone may declare an incident; over-declaring is preferred to silence. Note start time.
  • Classify using the matrix; open a dedicated incident channel/thread; record a running timeline (timestamps, actions, findings).
  • Contain: stop the bleeding first — maintenance mode, disable a failing integration via its kill-switch, revoke a leaked credential — before root-causing.
  • Communicate: per the update cadence above. For delivery incidents, Logistics informs affected vendors so plants are not packed for pickups that will not arrive.
  • Recover: restore service; for data incidents follow the Disaster Recovery Plan.
  • Close: the IC declares resolution only after verifying with a real end-to-end check (e.g., a test checkout), not just green dashboards.

6. Security and Personal Data Incidents

  • Preserve evidence (logs, snapshots) before remediation where feasible.
  • Rotate any credential suspected of exposure per the Password Policy and Security Standards.
  • Compliance assesses notification duties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and CERT-In reporting requirements; external notification wording requires legal review and leadership approval.

7. Post-Mortem Requirement

  • Every SEV1 and SEV2 incident requires a written post-mortem within 5 business days; SEV3 at the IC's discretion.
  • The post-mortem is blameless and must follow the standard template: summary, customer impact, timeline, root cause, what went well, what went poorly, action items with owners and due dates.
  • Action items are tracked to completion; an incident is not "done" until its actions are.

8. Responsibilities

  • Technology: maintains this plan, on-call awareness, and monitoring/alerting.
  • Customer Experience: maintains communication templates.
  • Compliance: maintains the regulatory notification assessment checklist.

9. Compliance

Failure to declare or escalate known SEV1/SEV2 conditions is a policy violation. Regulatory notifications are made only through Compliance and leadership.

Purpose

Defines how PlantAtHome plans, executes and closes internal audits of its operational and compliance processes, so that weaknesses in areas such as order fulfilment, vendor payouts, GST invoicing, refunds and data handling are found by us before they are found by customers, vendors or regulators.

Scope

Covers all internal audits of PlantAtHome processes and systems, including vendor nursery onboarding and payouts, inventory and plant-health checks, hyperlocal and courier dispatch, Razorpay payment reconciliation, GST invoicing, customer grievance handling, and access controls on admin systems. Statutory audits by external auditors are out of scope but findings feed the same corrective action process.

Audit Scope Selection

  • An annual audit plan is prepared by the Compliance Officer and approved by management before the start of each financial year.
  • Selection is risk-based: areas rated High or Critical in the Risk Management Framework are audited at least annually; Medium areas at least every two years; Low areas on rotation.
  • Trigger-based audits may be added mid-year following a serious incident (e.g. payment reconciliation gap, data incident, spike in dead-on-arrival plant complaints, vendor payout dispute).
  • Each audit has a written scope memo: process boundaries, period under review, sample sizes, and systems involved.

Audit Execution

  • The auditor must be independent of the process audited; where team size makes this impractical, the conflict is recorded and a reviewer from another function countersigns.
  • Evidence is gathered by sampling real records: order and shipment records, GST invoices, refund logs, vendor KYC files, courier booking records, consent logs. Sample sizes (DRAFT default: 25 records or 10% of the period volume, whichever is smaller) are stated in the scope memo.
  • Walkthroughs are performed with process owners; observed practice is compared against the written SOP and applicable rules (e.g. e-commerce disclosure rules, GST invoice content).
  • Fieldwork notes and evidence copies are retained in the audit file.

Findings and Reporting

  • Findings are graded: Critical (legal breach or money/data loss exposure), Major (control failure likely to cause customer, vendor or tax impact), Minor (procedural gap), Observation (improvement suggestion).
  • Each finding records: condition (what was found), criteria (what should be), cause, effect, and recommendation.
  • A draft report is shared with the process owner for factual accuracy within 5 working days of fieldwork completion; the final report goes to management within 10 working days.

Corrective Actions and Follow-up

  • Every Critical, Major and Minor finding must have a corrective action raised in the Corrective Action Process, with an owner and due date agreed in the closing meeting.
  • Critical findings require an interim containment step within 5 working days (DRAFT — configurable), even if the full fix takes longer.
  • The auditor performs a follow-up verification after the due date: re-testing a fresh sample, not merely accepting the owner's confirmation. A finding is closed only on verified evidence.
  • Open findings past due date are escalated per the Corrective Action Process escalation ladder.

Responsibilities

  • Compliance Officer: owns the audit plan, assigns auditors, issues reports, tracks follow-up.
  • Process Owners: provide records and access, respond to drafts, execute corrective actions.
  • Management: approves the annual plan, reviews Critical/Major findings quarterly.

Compliance

Obstruction of an audit, or knowingly providing incomplete records, is a disciplinary matter. Audit files are retained for 8 years (DRAFT — configurable).

Purpose

To ensure live plants dispatched by PlantAtHome and its vendor nurseries survive transit and arrive healthy, by standardizing hydration, ventilation, orientation, and seasonal transit windows, and to minimize dead-on-arrival (DOA) outcomes.

Scope

Applies to every shipment containing a live plant, on both hyperlocal and courier lanes, from any PlantAtHome fulfilment point or approved vendor nursery. FarmBox fresh produce follows its perishable rules in the Packaging Manual and ships hyperlocal only.

Definitions

  • DOA: a plant that arrives dead or damaged beyond recovery, as assessed from customer photos within 48 hours of delivery.
  • Transit window: the maximum time from dispatch to delivery a plant category may spend in transit for a given season.

Pre-Dispatch Preparation

  • Hydration: water plants 12–24 hours before dispatch so the root ball is moist but not waterlogged at packing; never water at the moment of packing — wet cartons collapse and soggy roots rot in transit (DRAFT timing, configurable).
  • Health check: only plants passing the inventory review health grade ship; visible pests, fungus, or wilt disqualify the unit.
  • Soil retention: bag the pot and top-dress with shredded paper or a soil cap so media stays in the pot when tilted.
  • Pruning: remove dead or damaged foliage before packing; it molds in a closed carton.

Ventilation and Orientation

  • Punch or verify ventilation holes near the top of the carton; foliage respires in transit and sealed cartons cook plants in Indian summer heat.
  • All plant cartons ship upright with This Side Up arrows on four faces; inserts or base strapping prevent tipping per the Packaging Manual.
  • Leave canopy clearance above foliage; compressed foliage bruises and blackens.
  • Hyperlocal riders are instructed at handover to keep the package upright and shaded; refuse handover to carriage that cannot keep the carton vertical.

Maximum Transit Windows by Season (DRAFT, configurable)

Monsoon (Jul–Sep)72 h48 h48 h
Winter (Nov–Feb, cold-wave zones)72 h48 hHold dispatch during cold waves
Moderate (Oct, Mar)96 h72 h48 h

Courier selection for plant shipments must choose a service whose expected transit fits the window; if no service fits, the order is held or moved to the hyperlocal lane, and the customer is informed on WhatsApp of the revised dispatch date. Destination weather alerts (heat wave, cold wave, cyclone) pause dispatch to affected pincodes.

DOA Prevention and Response

  • Dispatch early in the week for courier shipments so plants do not sit in warehouses over weekends (DRAFT rule, configurable).
  • Include a care card instructing the customer to unbox within hours of delivery, water lightly, and keep out of direct sun for 48 hours.
  • The delivery WhatsApp message repeats unboxing instructions and invites photos of any transit damage within 48 hours.
  • DOA claims are assessed from photos per the Reverse Logistics SOP; genuine DOA triggers replacement or refund without requiring return of the dead plant. Natural variation in size, shape, or leaf count is not a defect and is handled by Customer Experience with reference to the published customer policy.

Responsibilities

  • Fulfilment teams and vendor nurseries: hydration, health checks, compliant packing.
  • Logistics operations: transit-window enforcement, weather holds, courier selection.
  • Customer Experience: DOA assessment and resolution.
  • Vendor Operations: vendor training and DOA-rate monitoring per vendor.

Compliance

Plant shipments must respect any applicable state plant-movement and agricultural regulations for interstate shipping. Customer remedies for DOA follow the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and PlantAtHome's published policies.

Purpose

This SOP defines the end-to-end procedure for settling customer orders on the PlantAtHome platform, operated by Silvestrix Green LLP: from payment capture through Razorpay, to matching gateway settlements against orders, to posting entries in the financial ledger. It ensures every rupee received is traceable to an order, a settlement UTR, and a ledger entry.

Scope

Applies to all prepaid orders paid via Razorpay (cards, UPI, netbanking, wallets) and all Cash-on-Delivery (COD) orders remitted by courier and hyperlocal delivery partners. Covers all verticals: live plants, tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox, and corporate gifting orders.

Definitions

  • Capture: The point at which an authorized Razorpay payment is confirmed and funds are committed.
  • Settlement: The batched transfer of captured amounts (net of gateway fees and GST on fees) from Razorpay to the company bank account, identified by a UTR.
  • COD remittance: Periodic transfer of cash collected by delivery partners for COD orders.

Procedure — Capture

Payments are auto-captured on payment success. Finance verifies daily that no payments remain in an authorized-but-uncaptured state older than 24 hours; any such payment is escalated to Technology, since uncaptured authorizations auto-reverse and create phantom "paid" orders. COD orders enter the settlement pipeline only after delivery confirmation from the fulfilment partner.

Procedure — Settlement Retrieval and Matching

Each business day, Finance downloads the Razorpay settlement report (settlement ID, UTR, gross amount, fees, tax on fees, and constituent payment IDs). Each constituent payment ID is matched to a platform order via the stored gateway payment reference. Matching is three-level: payment ID to order, order amount to captured amount, and settlement net amount to the bank credit for that UTR.

For each matched settlement, Finance posts: gross receipts to the sales control account, gateway fees and GST on fees to expense accounts, and the net amount against the bank credit. Refunds initiated in the period are posted as contra entries referencing the original payment ID. Unmatched amounts are parked in a suspense account and must be cleared within 5 business days.

Exceptions

  • Partial settlements (Razorpay holds, on-hold flags) are logged and tracked to release.
  • Orders cancelled after capture but before dispatch are refunded per the Refund Approval Policy and excluded from revenue.
  • COD shortfalls versus delivered value are raised with the delivery partner within 7 days.

Responsibilities

  • Finance Manager: review of suspense items and sign-off on the daily settlement summary.

DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This policy sets password and authentication requirements for PlantAtHome staff, vendor operations users, and system accounts, so that access to the admin panel, cloud consoles, code repositories, courier and payment dashboards, and production infrastructure remains protected.

2. Scope

All employees, contractors, and vendor users of PlantAtHome-managed accounts and systems; all service and system accounts operated by the Technology team. Customer-facing authentication (phone OTP and social login on the storefront and app) is governed by product authentication design but must meet the spirit of this policy.

3. Password Requirements

  • Minimum length: 12 characters. Length is the primary control; there is no forced mix of character classes, but passwords must not be a single dictionary word, the word "plantathome", or a predictable pattern.
  • Passwords must be unique per system. Reusing a PlantAtHome password on any external site is prohibited.
  • Default, vendor-supplied, and shared onboarding passwords must be changed at first login.
  • Passwords must never be sent over email, WhatsApp, or chat, or written into tickets or documents.

4. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

  • MFA must be enabled wherever the system supports it, and is mandatory for: cloud infrastructure consoles, code hosting, CI/CD, payment gateway dashboards, courier partner dashboards, DNS/CDN, and admin accounts with user-management or finance permissions.
  • Authenticator apps or hardware keys are preferred; SMS-based MFA is acceptable only where no stronger option exists.
  • Loss of an MFA device must be reported to Technology the same day.

5. Rotation

  • Passwords are rotated on compromise or suspected compromise only — there is no calendar-based forced rotation, in line with current NIST guidance. Forced periodic rotation produces weaker, patterned passwords.
  • Mandatory rotation triggers: a breach notification affecting the account, credentials seen in logs or code, a phishing incident, departure of any person who knew a shared secret, or instruction from the Incident Response coordinator.
  • Rotation after a trigger must be completed within 24 hours (configurable) for production-affecting accounts.

6. Password Manager Storage

  • All work passwords must be stored in the company-approved password manager. Browsers' built-in save prompts, spreadsheets, notes apps, and paper are prohibited for work credentials.
  • Shared credentials that cannot be made individual (some partner dashboards allow only one login) must live in a shared vault with access limited to named roles, and must be rotated when anyone leaves that role.
  • The password manager master password must itself meet this policy and be protected by MFA.

7. System and Service Accounts

  • Service accounts use generated secrets of at least 32 random characters, stored per the Security Standards secrets-management rules, never in a personal vault.
  • Interactive login with service accounts is prohibited.

8. Responsibilities

  • Technology: provisions the password manager, enforces MFA on managed systems, executes rotations on compromise.
  • People: includes this policy in onboarding and offboarding checklists; offboarding triggers vault access removal and shared-credential rotation.
  • All staff: comply, and report suspected compromise immediately without fear of blame.

9. Compliance

Access may be suspended for accounts that do not meet MFA or storage requirements. Repeated or wilful violations are handled through the disciplinary process. Compromise events are handled under the Incident Response Plan.

Purpose

This policy sets the rules under which PlantAtHome (operated by Silvestrix Green LLP) runs discounts, coupon codes, seasonal sales, bundle offers, and other promotions, so that offers are applied fairly, consistently, and free of misuse.

Scope
