Discount Codes and Offers

  • Every offer has published terms at launch: eligible products or categories, minimum order value, maximum discount cap, validity window, eligible serviceable cities, and payment-method conditions (e.g., Razorpay card offers).
  • Because live plants are perishable and seasonally priced, PlantAtHome may exclude specific plants, FarmBox fresh produce, or vendor-fulfilled items from any promotion, and such exclusions will be stated in the offer terms.
  • Discounts apply to product value only unless the offer expressly covers delivery charges. GST is charged on the discounted price as reflected on the tax invoice.
  • Hyperlocal and courier delivery lanes may carry different offer eligibility where delivery cost structures differ; the applicable terms are shown at checkout.

Eligibility

  • Offers may be limited to specific customer segments: new customers (first order on a verified account), app-only users, specific cities, or corporate gifting accounts.
  • First-order offers are limited to one per person, determined by account, verified phone number, delivery address, and payment instrument. Creating multiple accounts to re-claim a first-order offer is misuse.
  • PlantAtHome employees and vendor staff may be excluded from public promotions where the offer terms say so.

One Code Per Order

Unless an offer explicitly states otherwise, only one discount code may be applied per order, and codes cannot be combined with each other or with automatic sale prices beyond what the checkout permits. Where a product already carries a sale price, the better of the two benefits applies unless the offer terms allow stacking.

Misuse Prevention

  • Misuse includes: multiple accounts for the same person, use of leaked or unpublished codes, automated or scripted redemption, placing orders with intent to cancel after capturing a benefit, and abuse of refund or plant-replacement processes to retain discounts.
  • PlantAtHome may, on reasonable evidence of misuse: reject the code at checkout, cancel affected orders before dispatch, reverse the discount on refund, and suspend the account after notice via registered email or WhatsApp.
  • Fraudulent payment activity connected to promotions is handled under the fraud provisions of the Terms of Service and may be reported to payment partners.

Modification Rights

  • PlantAtHome may modify, pause, or withdraw any promotion at any time for future orders, including where stock of live plants is exhausted, weather disrupts hyperlocal fulfilment, or a pricing or configuration error occurs.
  • Orders already placed and paid under a valid offer will be honoured, except where the order itself resulted from misuse or an obvious pricing error, in which case the customer will be offered a full refund to the original payment method.

  • Customer Experience: owns offer terms drafting, customer communication, and dispute resolution.
  • Vendor Operations: agrees funding splits and stock commitments for vendor-funded offers before launch.
  • Technology: code configuration, eligibility enforcement, and misuse detection.
  • Finance: discount budget approval, GST treatment, and promotion reconciliation.

Promotions must not be misleading and must comply with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and associated advertising guidelines. Offer creatives and terms require sign-off before publication per the internal approval matrix.

Purpose

This policy defines when and how PlantAtHome (operated by Silvestrix Green LLP) refunds money to customers, so that refunds are handled consistently, quickly, and in compliance with applicable Indian consumer protection and tax rules.

Scope

Applies to all orders placed on PlantAtHome channels (website, mobile app, WhatsApp-assisted orders) across all product categories — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce, and corporate gifting — whether fulfilled by PlantAtHome directly or by an approved nursery vendor, and delivered via hyperlocal or courier lanes.

Definitions

  • Refund trigger: an approved cancellation, an approved return or replacement resolved as a refund, a failed or duplicate payment, or an out-of-stock adjustment.

Eligibility

  • Cancellations approved under the Cancellation Policy before dispatch are eligible for a full refund.
  • Items approved under the Replacement Policy where a replacement is not feasible (e.g. plant variety out of season, vendor stock exhausted) are refunded in full including proportionate delivery charges.
  • Natural variation in live plants (size, leaf count, seasonal foliage) is not a refund ground; plant health issues are handled first through the Replacement Policy.
  • Delivery failure attributable to PlantAtHome or its courier/hyperlocal partner is refunded in full; failure due to an incorrect address or repeated customer unavailability may attract a deduction of the forward shipping cost (DRAFT value: actual cost, capped at ₹150, configurable).

Refund Method

Refunds are issued to the original instrument only, processed through the Razorpay refund API against the original payment. COD orders are refunded by bank transfer to a customer-verified account or UPI ID. Refunds are never issued in cash or to a third-party account. Where GST was invoiced, a corresponding credit note is issued against the original tax invoice.

Purpose

Because live plants are perishable and cannot be resold once shipped, PlantAtHome's primary remedy for order issues is replacement rather than return. This policy defines which issues qualify, what evidence is required, and how replacements are executed across PlantAtHome and vendor-nursery fulfilment.

Scope

Applies to all product categories delivered via hyperlocal or courier lanes. Where a replacement is not feasible, the case converts to a refund under the Refund Policy.

Definitions

  • Dead on arrival (DOA): a live plant that arrives with irreversible damage — fully wilted, rotted root ball, snapped main stem — reported within 24 hours of delivery.
  • Unboxing evidence: a continuous video starting before the sealed package is opened, showing the shipping label and the condition of contents as first revealed.

Eligible Scenarios

  • Damaged plants / transit damage: broken stems, crushed foliage, spilled and damaged root ball, or shattered pots caused in transit. Live plants are weather-sensitive; heat or cold stress visible at delivery is treated as transit damage.
  • Dead on arrival: must be reported within 24 hours of delivery with unboxing evidence. Minor leaf yellowing or drooping from transit stress is normal and typically recovers with care; it does not qualify as DOA on its own.
  • Wrong product: a different plant variety, tool, or item than ordered.
  • Wrong size: the delivered item is materially outside the listed size band (e.g. a plant listed as 2–3 ft arriving under 1 ft, or a planter of a different listed dimension). Natural variation within the listed band is not a defect.
  • Quality concerns: visible pests or disease at delivery, hollow or non-viable FarmBox produce, defective tools, or planters with manufacturing flaws.

Reporting Window

  • DOA and FarmBox fresh produce: within 24 hours of delivery.
  • All other scenarios: within 48 hours of delivery (DRAFT value, configurable).

Evidence Requirements

ScenarioRequired evidence

Wrong product or wrong sizePhotos of the item received alongside the invoice or order screen; for size disputes, a photo against a measuring tape or common reference object
Quality concerns (pests, disease, defects)Close-up photos of the affected area; short video where the issue is functional (e.g. a tool mechanism)

Evidence can be submitted in the app, by email, or on the PlantAtHome WhatsApp support number. Requests without required evidence are held for up to 48 hours pending submission.

Process and Timelines

  • Acknowledgement within 1 business day; decision within 2 business days of complete evidence.
  • Approved replacements ship within 3–5 business days, subject to plant availability, season, and weather-safe transit; hyperlocal replacements may ship faster.
  • Where physical return is needed (tools, planters, wrong product), PlantAtHome arranges reverse pickup at no cost; live plants generally need not be returned unless requested for vendor quality audit.
  • If the same item cannot be replaced, the customer chooses an equivalent alternative or a full refund.

Exclusions

  • Plant decline after delivery due to care conditions (overwatering, insufficient light, repotting shock).
  • Natural variation in size, shape, flowering stage, or foliage within the listed range.
  • Damage after delivery, or issues reported outside the windows above without a justified reason.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

1. Purpose

This standard sets the minimum technical security controls for PlantAtHome systems: the commerce API, storefront and admin applications, delivery microservices, databases, media storage, and supporting infrastructure. It exists to protect customer personal data, payment flows, vendor data, and platform availability.

2. Scope

All PlantAtHome production and staging environments, all code repositories, all cloud accounts (compute, container hosting, object storage, CDN), and all personnel and contractors who build or operate them.

3. Encryption in Transit

  • All external traffic — storefront, admin, mobile app, APIs, webhooks — must use HTTPS/TLS 1.2 or higher. Plain HTTP endpoints must redirect or be disabled.
  • Partner callbacks (payment gateway, courier partners, WhatsApp gateway) must be received only over TLS and verified by signature or HMAC secret.
  • Internal service-to-service calls crossing a network boundary must also use TLS; unencrypted links are permitted only within a single host (e.g., a local cache on the same box).

4. Encryption at Rest

  • Production databases and their backups must have storage-level encryption enabled.
  • Object storage buckets holding media and documents must use server-side encryption; buckets must not be publicly writable, and public reads flow only through the CDN.
  • Third-party courier and gateway credentials stored in the database (integration settings) must be application-encrypted, not plaintext columns.
  • Laptops used to access production must have full-disk encryption enabled.

5. Secrets Management

  • Secrets (API keys, database passwords, signing secrets, payment keys) live only in environment configuration, the deployment platform's secret store, or CI secret storage — never in source code, commit history, log output, or chat.
  • Each environment has its own secrets. Production payment credentials (live keys) must never be present in staging, and test keys must never remain in production.
  • Secret rotation is mandatory on suspected exposure, personnel departure, or vendor notification, and follows the Incident Response Plan.
  • Queue workers and long-running services must be restarted after secret or configuration changes so stale values are not held in memory.

6. Dependency and Patch Management

  • Application dependencies (Composer, npm/yarn) are updated on a monthly review cycle (configurable) and immediately for critical advisories affecting deployed packages.
  • Automated vulnerability alerts on repositories must be enabled and triaged within 5 business days; critical findings within 24 hours.
  • Operating system security patches on self-managed hosts are applied at least monthly, with emergency patching for actively exploited vulnerabilities.
  • Lockfiles are committed; production builds install from lockfiles only.

7. Environment Separation (Staging / Production)

  • Staging and production run distinct configurations, credentials, and third-party keys. Sandbox partner tokens (courier, payment) are staging-only.
  • Shared resources between staging and production (for example, a shared media bucket) are treated as a known risk: writes must go through the designated media service, and destructive operations require production-level approval until the environments are fully separated.
  • Production data may be copied to staging only after masking or removal of customer personal contact data.
  • Deployment to production occurs only through the approved CI/CD promotion workflow per the Change Management Policy — never by direct edits on production hosts.

8. Access Control and Logging

  • Administrative access uses role-based permissions with least privilege; server access goes through managed session tooling rather than shared SSH keys.
  • Authentication events, admin actions, and integration failures must be logged and retained for at least 90 days (configurable).

9. Responsibilities

  • Technology: implements and monitors these controls, runs the patch cycle, owns the secrets store.
  • All engineers: follow secure defaults, report gaps, never bypass controls for convenience.
  • Compliance: reviews this standard annually.

10. Compliance

Exceptions require written Technology leadership approval with an expiry date. Breaches of this standard are handled under the Incident Response Plan and may result in disciplinary action. Personal data incidents are assessed against the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

Purpose

Accurate inventory is the foundation of the PlantAtHome customer promise. A plant shown as available must actually be healthy, saleable, and physically present at the vendor nursery. Scope

Applies to all approved vendors supplying live plants, pots, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, and FarmBox produce, across all cities where the vendor is enabled for fulfilment.

Definitions

  • track_stock: the per-product flag that determines whether the platform decrements and enforces quantity on that listing.
  • Stockout cancellation: an order (or line item) cancelled because the vendor could not supply stock the platform showed as available.
  • Saleable stock: units meeting PlantAtHome quality standards — for live plants, free of visible pests, disease, and transit-disqualifying damage.

Stock Accuracy

  • Quantities on the platform must reflect physically available, saleable stock at all times. Reserved, wholesale-committed, or display stock must not be counted.
  • Live plants are perishable and weather-sensitive: after heat waves, heavy rain, pest events, or cold snaps, vendors must re-verify affected stock the same day and adjust quantities before accepting new orders.
  • Target accuracy: at least 98% of orders fulfillable from listed stock (DRAFT — configurable threshold, measured monthly).

track_stock Requirement

  • track_stock must be enabled on every vendor listing. Untracked listings (unlimited availability) are not permitted for live plants or FarmBox produce and may only be approved for made-to-order items by Vendor Operations exception.
  • When track_stock is enabled, the platform decrements quantity on order and blocks purchase at zero; vendors must not attempt to bypass this by re-listing duplicates.

Sync Cadence

  • Daily: full count confirmation for FarmBox produce before the day's cutoff.
  • Every 48 hours minimum: quantity review for live plants (DRAFT — configurable).
  • Immediately: on any known loss event (damage, disease, bulk walk-in sale, weather damage).
  • Weekly: reconciliation of platform quantities against a physical count for top-selling SKUs; Excel bulk updates route through the inventory review pipeline and take effect on approval.

Stockouts and Penalties

Purpose

This policy sets out how vendor prices are submitted, reviewed, and displayed on PlantAtHome, so that customers see lawful, honest, and competitive prices, and so that platform margins and city-level pricing are applied consistently and transparently.

Scope

Applies to all products supplied by approved nursery vendors and sold through the PlantAtHome master catalog, across all cities and both hyperlocal and courier fulfilment lanes. It covers base supply prices, displayed selling prices, discounts, and price changes.

Definitions

  • Supply price: the price the vendor charges PlantAtHome for a unit.
  • Selling price: the price displayed to customers after platform margin and any city-level adjustment.
  • MRP: maximum retail price printed or declared for pre-packaged goods.

Price Parity Expectations

  • Vendors must not offer the same product at a materially lower price through their own walk-in, WhatsApp, or other online channels for orders originated by PlantAtHome customers, and must not solicit platform customers off-platform to circumvent pricing.
  • Vendors may run their own retail business freely; parity applies to platform-originated demand, not the vendor's independent trade.
  • Where a vendor lists on other marketplaces, the supply price offered to PlantAtHome should be no worse than comparable wholesale terms (DRAFT — configurable expectation, subject to negotiation in the vendor agreement).

MRP and Legal Metrology Compliance

  • For pre-packaged commodities (fertilizers, seeds, potting media, tools, packed FarmBox items), the selling price must never exceed the declared MRP, and packages must carry the declarations required under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and its packaged commodities rules (net quantity, manufacturer/packer details, MRP inclusive of taxes, dates where applicable).
  • Live plants in nursery pots are generally not pre-packaged commodities; however, any plant sold in sealed retail packaging must comply as above.
  • Vendors are responsible for the accuracy of MRP and label data they submit; PlantAtHome may delist items with missing or non-compliant declarations.

Tax Treatment

All prices submitted must clearly state whether they are inclusive of GST and the applicable rate/HSN. Customer-facing prices are GST-inclusive. GST invoicing on customer orders is issued per the platform's invoicing configuration; vendors must hold valid GST registration where required and supply correct HSN codes at listing time.

Price Change Process

  • Vendors submit price changes through the vendor portal; changes route through the review pipeline and take effect only on approval.
  • Routine changes are reviewed within 2 business days (DRAFT — configurable). Increases above 20% or decreases below cost sanity thresholds are flagged for manual review.
  • Prices cannot be changed on units already ordered; the price at order time governs settlement.
  • Platform margins and city-level adjustments are applied by PlantAtHome on top of approved supply prices and are visible to the vendor in the settlement statement.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor Operations: review queue, parity monitoring, delisting decisions.
  • Finance: margin configuration, GST rate validation, settlement reconciliation.

Compliance

drafts.title: Vendor Product Image Standards
drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This standard defines the minimum photographic quality vendors must meet before a product listing is approved on PlantAtHome. Because we sell living plants, images carry a promise: the customer must receive a plant reasonably resembling what was photographed, allowing for natural variation in a live product. Consistent, honest imagery reduces disputes, quality-fail claims, and returns on both hyperlocal and courier lanes.

Scope

Applies to all images submitted by approved nursery vendors and by PlantAtHome's own catalog team for live plants, pots and planters, gardening tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, and FarmBox produce. Applies to new listings and image updates via the vendor catalogue and the inventory review pipeline.

Technical Requirements

  • Resolution: minimum 1200px on the shortest edge; JPEG or PNG; no visible compression artifacts.
  • Background: plain white or neutral (light grey/beige) background for the primary image. Lifestyle backgrounds are permitted only for secondary images.
  • Lighting: even, diffused daylight or studio lighting; no harsh shadows, colour casts, or flash hotspots on foliage.
  • Framing: the product must occupy at least 70% of the frame, fully in focus, with the pot base visible for potted plants.

Authenticity Requirements

  • The photograph must be of a real plant actually representative of the stock being sold — not a stock photo, catalogue image, or render — unless the listing is an accessory or tool for which manufacturer imagery is permitted with rights.
  • No misleading enhancement: no artificial saturation of leaf colour, no compositing of flowers onto non-flowering stock, no removal of natural leaf marks that would materially change buyer expectations.
  • Plant size shown must match the size class listed (small/medium/large). A scale reference (pot size in cm) must be stated in the listing.
  • Seasonal state must be honest: a plant sold in dormancy or pre-bloom must not be shown in full bloom as the primary image.

Required Angles

  • Primary: full front view on neutral background.
  • Secondary: 45-degree angle showing form and fullness.
  • Detail: close-up of foliage/flower/graft point as relevant.
  • Scale: plant beside a common reference or with measurement overlay (text overlays otherwise prohibited).
  • For ceramic/fragile items: base and glaze detail. For FarmBox produce: representative batch photo, not a hand-picked single specimen.

Rejection Reasons

  • Resolution below 1200px, blur, or heavy compression.
  • Cluttered or dark background on the primary image.
  • Watermarks, borders, promotional text, phone numbers, or third-party branding.
  • Stock or AI-generated imagery presented as the actual plant.
  • Enhancement that misrepresents colour, size, health, or bloom state.
  • Image does not match the listed variety, pot type, or size class.

Responsibilities

  • Vendors: supply compliant images and refresh imagery when stock materially changes.
  • Catalog/Review team: approve or reject via the inventory review pipeline with the rejection reason recorded.
  • Vendor Operations: maintain this standard and train onboarding vendors.

Compliance

Listings with non-compliant images will be held in review and not published. Repeated submission of misleading imagery is a misdescription violation under the Vendor Penalty Matrix and may trigger a quality-score deduction. Requirements align with fair-representation expectations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

drafts.html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a working draft generated for internal review and must be approved by authorized management and legal counsel before publication or enforcement.

Purpose

This procedure defines the vendor-side steps for handling customer returns: receiving reverse pickups, inspecting returned goods, deciding restock versus disposal, and receiving or issuing credit. Because most returns involve live plants, speed and honest condition assessment matter more than in general retail — a plant that sits in a return carton for three days has no salvage value.

Scope

Applies to all vendor-fulfilled orders where PlantAtHome approves a return, replacement, or refund claim, on both hyperlocal and courier lanes. Customer-facing eligibility rules live in the customer Returns and Refunds Policy; this SOP covers only the vendor-side flow. FarmBox produce is refund-only (never physically returned) and is out of scope for physical handling.

Procedure

1. Return Notification

  • PlantAtHome approves the customer claim and creates a return; the vendor is notified via the vendor portal and WhatsApp with the order reference, item(s), claim reason, and customer-submitted photos.
  • The reverse pickup is booked by PlantAtHome from the customer's address back to the vendor nursery — the vendor is the drop point, not the pickup point.

2. Reverse Pickup Receipt

  • The vendor must be ready to receive the return during declared operating hours and acknowledge receipt in the portal within 24 hours of physical delivery (DRAFT — configurable).
  • On receipt, photograph the parcel exterior before opening, then the contents. These photos are mandatory evidence for any condition dispute.

3. Inspection

  • Inspect within 24 hours of receipt. Live plants degrade in transit packaging; delayed inspection forfeits the vendor's right to dispute condition.
  • Record in the portal: item identity match, plant health (pests, disease, rot, breakage), pot/accessory condition, completeness (pot, saucer, freebies).
  • Classify the outcome: Restockable, Rehabilitate (plant recoverable after nursery care but not immediately saleable), or Dispose.

4. Restock or Dispose

  • Restockable: return to saleable stock and update platform quantity (track_stock) the same day.
  • Rehabilitate: hold out of platform stock; may be re-listed only when it again meets Image and quality standards.
  • Dispose: diseased or pest-infested plants must be disposed of away from healthy nursery stock to prevent spread; photograph before disposal.

5. Credit and Cost Allocation

  • Vendor-fault returns (dead/damaged on arrival due to plant health or packaging, wrong item, misdescription): the customer refund and reverse logistics cost are deducted from the vendor's next settlement per the Settlement Policy.
  • Platform/courier-fault returns (transit damage with compliant packaging, delivery failure): no vendor deduction; a restockable item is simply returned to stock, and a non-restockable one is credited to the vendor at supply price (DRAFT — configurable).
  • Customer-remorse returns (where permitted): item returns to vendor stock; cost allocation per the customer policy.
  • Fault classification is made by Vendor Operations from claim evidence and inspection records; vendors may dispute within the 7-day settlement dispute window.

Responsibilities

  • Vendors: receive, photograph, inspect, and disposition returns within timelines; keep quantities accurate.
  • Vendor Operations: classify fault, adjudicate disputes, monitor return rates per vendor.
  • Logistics: book and track reverse pickups; supply pickup scan evidence.

Compliance

Missed acknowledgement or inspection windows waive condition disputes for that return. Refusing legitimate reverse pickups or restocking non-compliant plants is a violation under the Vendor Penalty Matrix. Customer remedies are honoured consistent with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

  • Normal wear and tear, rust from outdoor exposure on tools, or damage from misuse, modification, or improper storage.

  • Breakage of pots and planters from impact, frost, or overloading after delivery.
  • Natural variation in living products — size, shape, flowering, foliage colour.
  • Transit damage, which is handled under the Replacement Policy, not warranty.

Making a Warranty Claim

  • Raise a claim via the app, email, or the PlantAtHome WhatsApp support number, quoting the order ID from the GST invoice.
  • Provide photos (and video for functional faults) showing the defect.
  • For manufacturer-warranted tools, PlantAtHome shares the invoice and warranty card details and connects the customer to the manufacturer's service channel; where the manufacturer requires it, the original packaging or warranty card must be retained.
  • Approved PlantAtHome-serviced claims are resolved by repair, replacement, or refund (in that order of preference) within 7 business days of approval (DRAFT, configurable).
